question: A certain sum of money triples itself in 8 years at simple interest. In how many years will it become four times itself?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In SI, interest ∝ time

Triple ⇒ interest = 2P in 8 years

Four times ⇒ interest = 3P

Time ∝ interest ⇒ time = 8 × (3/2)

**∴ Answer = 12 years**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A sum becomes 3 times in 8 years at simple interest

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ When amount becomes 3P ⇒ SI = 2P

⇒ 2P = (P × R × 8) ÷ 100

⇒ 2 = (R × 8) ÷ 100

⇒ R = 200 ÷ 8 = 25

⇒ For 4P ⇒ SI = 3P

⇒ 3P = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 3 = (25 × T) ÷ 100

⇒ T = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Growth

In SI, interest increases linearly with time.

Multiplication Rule

If amount becomes n times, SI = (n − 1)P.

Direct Proportion

Time ∝ Interest when rate is constant.
